scope: Partial human reconstruction of RH and Dirichlet GRH, with complete dependency chains as the organizing unit. HP1–HP6 prove the literal characteristic-zero polynomial highest-weight, absolute irreducibility, classification, original-field descent and full wt_weights supplier by Gaussian elimination and a factorial pairing. VW1–VW4 close the same-field cohomological assembly from JointWin and ThmBc to VWinAt, and from ThmBab, PointHV and ThmBcFree to fixed-pair windows with QP22. WB1–WB8 close the arithmetic-gap-to-character-window chain, including ramification, biased Fourier averaging, moving cutoffs and the exact scalar exponent, then join the already complete AN2/AN3/GH6 analytic endpoint. DA1–DA2 prove the finite uniform family join and the conditional global-link assembly, with a semantic AND/OR obligation map. The actual common arithmetic family/gap, deep cohomological bounds, genuine theta/local installation, spectral/global operator estimates, integral metric transport and congruence denominators remain explicit inputs. No complete self-contained human RH/Dirichlet-GRH proof, Lean build or independent kernel replay is claimed.
range_convention: All line numbers are one-based inclusive. Ranges may include trailing comments or namespace endings before the next declaration.
status_convention: Source translations retain their hypotheses. Derived alternatives have written mathematical proofs but have not been replayed in Lean. Remaining inputs have not been supplied with complete human proofs.

claims.title: The exact complementary count supplies the required rank fraction

claims.title: Actual pair span, retained degree blocks and exact tensor factorization
claims.statement: The actual localizer is supported on plane vector variables. A compatible low-digit block factors as A_* tensor G_*, and normal coefficient extraction after the projector is a scalar multiple of A_*.

claims.title: All selected normal prefix types inherit the original maximum-weight cutoffs
claims.statement: Canonical isotypic projectors for nested/disjoint prefixes commute. Joint-isotypic vectors span each finite-degree space, so the literal IsJProj condition determines the product projector uniquely. A nonzero selected normal vector therefore has each selected type present; its largest coordinate is bounded by the original segment normal-prefix maximum. No integral direct sum or projector-denominator estimate is used.
claims.background: Ordinary characteristic-zero complete reducibility and highest-weight extremal-weight facts, already used in v0_5 PG/IW. The report supplies the precise commutation, uniqueness, homogeneous-filtering and prefix identification argument.

Signed label costs dS+dV<=kNsP and the individual determinant order s_x prove every fine gap, threshold and normal-order condition, with correct even/odd prefix indices and supports.

Local label e is late-supported and every exponent is <P_j.

claims.statement: The signed prefix coordinate width is at most D, yielding HypP, HypE and HypW with e1=binom(r,2)Nat.log_p(D+r-1). HypE is the matching smaller-group type projector on a fixed full weight. Highest-vector generation works on an entire isotypic module with multiplicities and requires no integral irreducible splitting.

claims.source_relation: The multiplicity-space extension of IW3 is proved explicitly. The Hom height is the difference of two weights at one coordinate, not a difference of coordinates within one weight.

claims.statement: The literal XSp direct sum is stable under EX. A direct first-weight argument bypasses rational-surjectivity/Omega injectivity. Generic W-coordinate evaluation gives o<=c+D_early, and all auxiliary weight coordinates lie in [-D_early,c+2D_early], so the width is <=4D. The formal U-flow proves root divided-power integrality for every integer c.

claims.title: Construct the literal standard coefficient ring and all its quadratic-setting properties
claims.statement: For p>=5 prime and even f>=2, O_s=W(F_(p^(2f)))[omega]/(omega^2-p) is the complete DVR with uniformizer omega, residue cardinal p^(2f), a finite rank-four structural map from W(F_(p^f)), compatible Frobenius period f, and a square root of every integer. BC2 proves the complete-DVR integral-closure and chosen-place construction, using only standard characteristic-zero separability, trace linear algebra and number-field integer-ring facts.

claims.source_relation: Residue-basis lifting proves rank two for W2/W, and the opposite-parity valuation gives the quadratic DVR directly. The source name does not mean O_s/W is unramified: its ramification and residue degrees are both two.

claims.title: Faithful descent and exact finite-free lattice, dual, intersection and valuation transport
claims.statement: For a finite compatible inclusion R->S of DVRs, S has an R-basis beginning with 1. All R-defined submodules in a K-space extend coordinatewise, so arbitrary intersections, kernels and lattice duals commute, inclusions descend, and saturation/ranks are preserved. Integer valuations and module lengths scale by the ramification index; p-normalized valuations and lengths do not change.
assumptions: All coefficient rings in the application are DVR domains with compatible fraction-field embeddings. The source unramified ring W, its field Q, Frobenius and lattice edges stay fixed.

BC1 uses the literal p>=5, f>=2 and Even f. Its field/Witt-vector existence and Teichmuller expansions are declared classical background; the required finite, quadratic, square-root and residue properties are proved in the report.
BC2 proves the complete-DVR integral-closure and chosen-place construction, using only standard characteristic-zero separability, trace linear algebra and number-field integer-ring facts.
CB1-CB2 and CB7 are prior proved integral tableau-basis/change-of-basis results; no integral semisimplicity premise is introduced.

The full globally compatible family is not constructed here. The pointwise StdSubAt conclusion applies to recC data or supplied RingCompatibleAt identifications. Eventual compatible ring data can come from IsRecCEv or directly from GroupCompatibilityFamily; neither route is required simultaneously with the other.
The formulas using normalized p-valuations concern the mixed-characteristic setting with p nonzero and nonunit; zero is treated by the usual value +infinity.
claims.source_relation: The source needs only forward lattice membership. The report explicitly proves the stronger arbitrary-intersection and descent statements by finite freeness, not by flatness alone. Duals are field-valued algebraic duals, not trace duals; no different is omitted.

claims.title: Temporary-family selection and actual fixed-pair reconstruction for every position
claims.statement: Build a temporary family from supplied arbitrary-pair point constructors and numerical records, apply GW5 uniformly, and transfer the chosen pair to its original host. Invoke the universal point constructor again for this same pair and all u0<n. Prove every Pt.Same field, including the lifted offsets from fills and Val.hc, canonical kappaI, the whole natural-input ep function, code labels and cover; all resulting points satisfy WallPt.
assumptions: Literal HostExQW/HostGood with RankVal, canonical q0 and any additional retained host predicate.
Std C and C.GK.Nonneg; the actual ObjC/ObjCP point constructor for every admissible pair and all u0, with its uniform nested thresholds.
Supplied initial window pair, admissible injective code, and actual NumAt records for temporary and final points.
The temporary family meets the already stated GI/GII/GJ/GW5 hypotheses; its constants and J are fixed before the scale.
claims.new_human_argument: Reconstruct the full equality record rather than cite same_of_from as a black box; the actual Hodge filling equation yields the offset formula. State the two constructor calls and nested constant order explicitly.
remaining_inputs: Arithmetic host existence with all HostGood clauses, including the required top-set properties.
Actual universal input-pair point construction, its geometric records and numerical supply; these are not asserted proved by HW2.
The nondegree portions of KitCPW, such as the thick-set and chosen-bad-prime assertions, require their separate named suppliers.

claims.title: Explicit unramified lifting and exact completion comparison
claims.statement: For an unramified number-field prime P over p of residue degree m, construct a Good embedding into Q_m=Frac(W(F_(p^m))). Conversely, every such Good embedding identifies the actual completion with Q_m and its integer ring with W_m, compatibly with the original number field.
assumptions: The host is supplied: E/Q is Galois CM with its stated abelian Galois group, conjugation, complex embedding, conductor and arithmetic Frobenius law. This component does not construct the host or prove abundance of suitable primes.

Classical background is stated in report.txt: finite fields; the Witt rings and Teichmuller expansions already used in BC1; number-field integer rings finite over Z and Dedekind; DVR localization/completion; lying over; and the elementary inertia identity |I_P|=e_P.

BC1-BC3 are prior proved results supplying the actual finite coefficient extension, its chosen-place embedding and the exact ramification scaling. Their proofs are reused, not reasserted as new LI claims.

The global class-rank equality and comparison-lattice identification remain separate. No full IsLocalFamily, GroupCompatibilityAll, linked family, RH or GRH conclusion is asserted here.
For the forward direction the prime is unramified; for the converse the three literal Good clauses are given. The converse itself implies unramifiedness.
